messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired 2 SEV-2 2 region=eu-west-1 2 inference-pool-d 2 node flapping + kubelet restarts. Alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/1788882222

incident-bot: Quick summary: ~25% of inference pods restarting or NotReady across nodes node-303, node-307, node-312. Kernel logs show GPU timeouts (Xid=31) and containerd OOM events. Traffic degradation observed for high-concurrency endpoints.

Ana (oncall): I'm taking the page. First question: is fallback routing already enabled? Any immediate SLA hits?

CS-bot: Customer reports: elevated 5xx for eu-west embeddings and text-gen. Two customers escalated to high priority. Tickets: ZD#48002, ZD#48009.

Ruth (prod): We're seeing p99 latency spike from 1.1s -> 3.8s for rwd-7b-highconcurrency. Error rate up to 14% at peak. Fallback pools are at 70% capacity. Recommend we shift weight to us-west warm pool and throttle large-batch requests.

Diego (infra): collecting logs. node-307 dmesg snippet: 
```
May 20 03:11:23 node-307 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus.
May 20 03:11:24 node-307 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 9821 (inferd) score 1023 or sacrifice child
May 20 03:11:25 node-307 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```

Diego (infra): It looks like a combination of GPU reset + large memory pressure causing kubelet OOMs. I'll cordon the noisy nodes and drain them. Ana, can you flip routing while I do that?

Ana (oncall): Doing routing change now: `redwoodctl route set inference-pool-d --weights primary:20,fallback-eu:50,fallback-us:30 --gradual 30s`

ops-runbook-bot: Suggested runbook: node-flap-gpu-reset-v5. Steps: cordon/drain -> increase fallback -> try driver reload -> if modprobe fails use `fuser -k /dev/nvidia*` -> reboot -> replace node. Also suggests enabling temporary kubelet eviction thresholds.

Diego (infra): Cordoning nodes: `kubectl cordon node-303 node-307 node-312` then `kubectl drain node-307 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force -n inference`. Evicting inference pods now.

Ruth (prod): Noted. Also applying model variant downgrade for heavy endpoints: `redwoodctl model set rwd-7b-highconcurrency --variant reduced-memory` in eu-west to reduce memory footprint.

Ana (oncall): CS notified: "We've isolated noisy nodes and are routing traffic to fallback. Engineers are investigating GPU driver resets and memory pressure. Next update in 20 minutes."

Diego (infra): Attempting driver reload on node-307: `systemctl stop nvidia-persistenced && fuser -k /dev/nvidia* || true && modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia && systemctl start nvidia-persistenced`

Diego (infra): Driver unload failed initially with "resource busy". Found stale containerd processes still holding /dev/nvidia*; force-killed them and retried. Modprobe completed and `nvidia-smi` now responds. Rebooting node to clear kernel state.

ops-runbook-bot: Note: if more than 2 GPU resets occur in 15m, consider cross-region capacity increase and optional SEV-1 escalation. Current resets=3 in 12m window.

Ana (oncall): Given that, I've temporarily increased us-west warm pool: `kubectl scale deployment/infer-warm-usw --replicas=25 -n inference` and set LB to send 35% of new requests to us-west.

Diego (infra): node-307 rebooted and rejoined cluster; kubelet now healthy. node-303 still Q'ing kubelet restarts, scheduling replacement if it fails next health-check.

Ruth (prod): After routing and model downgrades, error-rate dropped to 4% and p95 latency back to 1.3s. Good trend. We'll keep throttles on large batches: `redwoodctl quota set tenant/epsilon --max-batch-size=6`

Diego (infra): node-312 shows repeated `kubelet[pid]: fatal error: runtime: out of memory` in journalctl before restart. I'm going to adjust kubelet cgroup reservations on that node template and push a cluster-wide conservative kube-reserved patch to avoid kubelet being OOMed.

Ana (oncall): Ops-runbook: do it but be careful with rolling changes. Schedule only on new nodes and patch one AZ first.

Diego (infra): Will do staged patch: `kubectl apply -f kubelet-reserved-patch.yaml --selector=zone=eu-west-1a` then monitor. Also adding node annotation `redwood.io/avoid-gpu-scheduler=true` on nodes showing GPU resets to prevent new GPU pods until cleared.

CS-bot: CS update: customers ZD#48002 and ZD#48009 notified of mitigation and ETA for postmortem. They reported degraded SLA window 03:10-03:28 UTC.

Ruth (prod): Can we capture artifacts for postmortem? Please collect: full dmesg, `nvidia-smi -q`, kubelet journal, containerd events, and model allocation traces for affected pods. ops-runbook-bot, please attach runbook checklist to incident.

ops-runbook-bot: Checklist attached and artifact list added to INC-1788882222. Recommend also capturing kernel oops and firmware versions.

Diego (infra): node-303 failed health-check after restart; we've marked it unschedulable and requested replacement: `redwoodctl node replace node-303 --reason=gpu-reset-oom`
I also took a snapshot of /var/log/dmesg and AMI for forensic imaging.

Ana (oncall): Handoff plan: I'll hand to Diego for follow-up at 03:35 UTC for node replacements and postmortem. I'll remain on-call for 30m in case of SEV escalation.

Ruth (prod): Final metrics: eu-west error-rate steady at ~1.5%, p95 latency ~1.2s after 03:32. CS to send final customer follow-up after postmortem.

Diego (infra): I'll own the postmortem and the remediation PR to pin a known-good driver on eu-west pools and add kubelet memory guard. Also will propose autoscaler policy to avoid packing >X GPU pods per node based on recent memory usage.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=SEV-2, mitigations applied, next_update=03:55 UTC, incident_id=INC-1788882222. Thread archived to tracker when status=mitigated.

CS-bot: Logging SLA impacts for billing team.

Ana (oncall): Leaving channel at 03:35 UTC; handoff to Diego complete. Thanks team.
